name: Armando
bio: A young Roman whom Wilde knew in April 1900, described to Robert Ross as 'a very smart elegant young Roman Sporus' and, at greater length, as being 'so absurdly like the Apollo Belvedere that I feel always as if I was Winckelmann when I am with him'. Wilde gave him up over the cost of his clothes, took up his best friend instead, and had forgiven him within a fortnight. He survives under a first name only.
bio_note: HE IS THE BEST-DOCUMENTED OF THE ROME COHORT: two folios, both read at the page, one of them carrying a sustained physical description of a kind Wilde wrote about almost nobody else this late. 'Sporus' was Nero's boy-favourite and is not an ambiguous word in Wilde's vocabulary; 'Winckelmann' is Johann Joachim Winckelmann, to whom Pater devoted a chapter of The Renaissance and whose name in this circle carries the whole freight of adult male desire for young men modelled on Greek sculpture. The gap existed because only Armando has his own General Index entry ('Armando (boy), 1182, 1184'); the other two appear inside the same paragraphs and are indexed nowhere.
